summary: Siskiyou lookout on Mount Emily, Curry County: cupola cabin dated 1922, rebuilt after 1925 lightning, 20 ft L-4 tower 1948-1973; a 1942 bombing was spotted from it.

facts.design: L-4 tower (1948), replacing a D-6 cupola cabin
facts.status_note: Register says the L-4 tower was removed in 1973; firelookout.com says it was destroyed that year.

access.note: A Forest Service trail built in 1975 leads visitors to a platform over the Wheeler Ridge bombing site. No source describes access to the old summit lookout.

visit.trail_note: Forest Service trail to the Wheeler Ridge bombing site, ending at a viewing platform.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says it was removed in 1973; firelookout.com says it was destroyed in 1973. The story says removed and reports both.

The register dates the D-6 cupola cabin to 1922. A September 1922 Siskiyou Bulletin item says the lookout had not yet been constructed, and a 1923 Gold Beach item describes a new building at the station. The story gives the register's date and notes the dispute.
The register and firelookout.com give 20 feet (6.1 m). A 1963 item in The World describes a forty-foot tower. The story and facts use 20 feet.
Spelled Gardner in Wikipedia and Clio and Gardiner in the Herald and News account quoted on the lookout site. The story uses Gardner and notes the other spelling.

firelookout.com gives 7 miles northeast of Brookings for the lookout; the Herald and News account gives nine miles; Clio places the bombing site nineteen miles east of Brookings. The story uses only the firelookout figure.

notes_for_editor: Brief coordinates (42.10237, -124.1528) match the NGS-based coordinates in Wikipedia's Mount Emily article; the west_us_lookouts point (42.0698, -124.1059) is the outlier. The 1922 cabin date and the 1973 end are both disputed. No read source describes the summit today; the Clio entry describes the bombing site, not the lookout footprint. An AllTrails page returned 403. A YouTube description seen only as a search snippet says wildfire destroyed the tower; it was not read and is not used. The 1966 recruiting notice on the weebly page is left out as a plan, not a staffing record. Wikipedia tags its 'not dropped from the correct height' and 'two men' sentences [citation needed]; the story keeps both under footnote 4, so they should be checked against a better source before the story is final.
